steps.prompt: One sign at the pool says: “The pool was clean every morning.” Another says: “The pool is cleaned every morning.” Which sign tells you someone does a job? What tiny change makes the difference?

cards.title: The passive recipe
cards.body: Passive = a form of BE + a PAST PARTICIPLE. The form of be shows the tense; the participle never changes. The be verb agrees with the new subject (the receiver): the cookie was eaten, the cookies were eaten.

cards.title: Every tense
cards.text:
Present: The pool is cleaned. / The pools are cleaned.
Past: The pool was cleaned. / The pools were cleaned.
Future: The pool will be cleaned.
Present progressive: The pool is being cleaned.
Past progressive: The pool was being cleaned.
Present perfect: The pool has been cleaned.
Past perfect: The pool had been cleaned.
With can, must or should: The pool must be cleaned.
cards.note: Only the be part changes. “Cleaned” stays the same in every line.

cards.title: Irregular participles
cards.text: take → taken · write → written · break → broken · choose → chosen · eat → eaten · give → given · build → built · sing → sung · steal → stolen · find → found
cards.note: The passive needs the participle, never the simple past: “was taken”, not “was took”.

cards.title: The most common slip
cards.telling: The poem was wrote by my sister.
cards.showing: The poem was written by my sister.
cards.note: Test it with “have”: you’d say “I have written”, not “I have wrote”. The form that fits after have is the one for the passive.

prompts: Which passive tense was hardest to build? Write the recipe for it in your own words.
Which irregular participle do you mix up most? Make up a trick to remember it.
